# Demographic and Nutritional Determinants of Serum Triglyceride Levels

## Dataset Formation

```{r dataset}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

# Load files
exam <- read.csv("bloodpressure.csv")
bmx  <- read.csv("bodymeasures.csv")
day1 <- read.csv("day1diet.csv")
day2 <- read.csv("day2diet.csv")
demo <- read.csv("demographics.csv")
ldl <- read.csv("ldl.csv")
hdl <- read.csv("hdl.csv")

# Diet: sum within person-day, then average across days
nutr <- c("KCAL","PROT","CARB","FIBE","SUGR","SFAT","SODI","POTA","ALCO")

day1_person <- day1 %>%
  filter(DR1DRSTZ == 1) %>%
  group_by(SEQN) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(paste0("DR1I", nutr)), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^DR1I", "", .x), starts_with("DR1I"))

day2_person <- day2 %>%
  filter(DR2DRSTZ == 1) %>%
  group_by(SEQN) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(paste0("DR2I", nutr)), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^DR2I", "", .x), starts_with("DR2I"))

diet <- bind_rows(day1_person, day2_person) %>%
  group_by(SEQN) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(kcal = KCAL, protein = PROT, carbs = CARB, fiber = FIBE,
         sugar = SUGR, satfat = SFAT, sodium = SODI, potassium = POTA,
         alcohol = ALCO)

# Merge
dat <- demo %>%
  left_join(exam, by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bmx,  by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(ldl %>% dplyr::select(SEQN, LBXTLG, LBDLDL), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(diet, by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(hdl %>% dplyr::select(SEQN, LBDHDD), by = "SEQN")

# Select variables, build blood pressure, rename, make factors
dat_clean <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(SEQN, RIDAGEYR, RIAGENDR, RIDRETH3, DMDEDUC2, INDFMPIR,
                BMXBMI, protein, carbs, fiber, satfat, sodium, potassium, 
                alcohol, LBDLDL, LBXTLG, LBDHDD,
                BPXOSY1, BPXOSY2, BPXOSY3, BPXODI1, BPXODI2, BPXODI3) %>%
  mutate(
    sbp = rowMeans(cbind(BPXOSY1, BPXOSY2, BPXOSY3), na.rm = TRUE),
    dbp = rowMeans(cbind(BPXODI1, BPXODI2, BPXODI3), na.rm = TRUE),
    sbp = ifelse(is.nan(sbp), NA, sbp),
    dbp = ifelse(is.nan(dbp), NA, dbp),
    DMDEDUC2 = ifelse(DMDEDUC2 %in% c(7, 9), NA, DMDEDUC2)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-BPXOSY1, -BPXOSY2, -BPXOSY3, -BPXODI1, -BPXODI2, -BPXODI3) %>%
  rename(
    id = SEQN,
    age = RIDAGEYR,
    sex = RIAGENDR,
    race_ethnicity = RIDRETH3,
    education = DMDEDUC2,
    income_ratio = INDFMPIR,
    bmi = BMXBMI,
    sat_fat = satfat,
    ldl = LBDLDL,
    hdl = LBDHDD,
    triglyceride = LBXTLG
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c(1, 2),
                 labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    race_ethnicity = factor(race_ethnicity,
                            levels = c(3, 1, 2, 4, 6, 7),
                            labels = c("NH White", "Mexican American", "Other Hispanic",
                                       "NH Black", "NH Asian", "Other/Multiracial")),
    education = factor(education, levels = 1:5,
                       labels = c("<9th grade", "9-11th grade", "HS/GED",
                                  "Some college/AA", "College grad+"))
  )

# Adults only, drop missing
dat_final <- dat_clean %>%
  filter(age >= 20, age <= 65) %>%
  na.omit()

write.csv(dat_final, "dat_final.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Triglyceride Summary Statistics

```{r table-response}
x <- dat_final$triglyceride
q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
iqr <- q[2] - q[1]

trig_tab <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("n", "Missing", "Min", "Q1", "Median", "Mean", "Q3", "Max",
                "SD", "IQR", "Outliers"),
  Value = c(sum(!is.na(x)), sum(is.na(x)), min(x, na.rm = TRUE), q[1],
            median(x, na.rm = TRUE), mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), q[2],
            max(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
            iqr, sum(x < q[1] - 1.5 * iqr | x > q[2] + 1.5 * iqr, na.rm = TRUE))
)
trig_tab$Value <- round(trig_tab$Value, 2)

knitr::kable(trig_tab, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Summary of Triglycerides (mg/dL)")
```

#Is it suitable for linear model? (independent and continuous?) Since each person is assigned an ID number we are able to verify independence of observations since each person appears only once in our final dataset. Additionally, the triglyceride is continuous, but has an apparent right skew that will need to be corrected through a transformation. The 0 null values in the triglyceride variable is also important for maintaining all 1419 observations throughout any calculations.

## Numerical Predictor Summary Statistics

```{r table-numerical-predictors}
num_vars <- c("age", "bmi", "income_ratio", "protein", "carbs", "fiber")

pred_tab <- t(sapply(dat_final[num_vars], function(x) {
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q[2] - q[1]
  c(Missing  = sum(is.na(x)),
    Min      = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1       = q[[1]],
    Median   = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean     = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3       = q[[2]],
    Max      = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD       = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Outliers = sum(x < q[1] - 1.5 * iqr | x > q[2] + 1.5 * iqr, na.rm = TRUE))
}))

knitr::kable(round(pred_tab, 2),
  caption = "Summary of Numeric Predictors")
```

# Any skews, high variances, missing values, outliers?

For all predictors, there are no missing values. The income_ratio and age predictors are roughly symmetric, BMI has a sight right skew indicating some high-end outliers. Protein, carbs, and fiber all have right skews indicating high-end outliers and the need for transformations to adjust for this. The categorical variables are all fairly representative of the American population with the ratio in the sample being comparable to U.S. census data.

## Categorical Predictor Summary Statistics

```{r table-categorical}
cat_vars <- c("sex", "race_ethnicity", "education")

cat_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cat_vars, function(v) {
  t <- table(dat_final[[v]], useNA = "ifany")
  data.frame(Variable = v, Level = names(t), n = as.vector(t),
             Percent = round(100 * as.vector(t) / sum(t), 1))
}))

knitr::kable(cat_tab, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Summary of Categorical Predictors")
```

## Interaction Term Analysis

```{r interaction plots}
num_vars <- c("age", "bmi", "income_ratio", "protein", "carbs", "fiber")

dat_long <- pivot_longer(dat_final, cols = all_of(num_vars),
                         names_to = "predictor", values_to = "value")

ggplot(dat_long, aes(x = value, y = triglyceride, color = education)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ predictor, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_minimal()
```

It apprears that the relationship between carbohydrates and triglycerides differ based on education Let's test this further.

```{r interaction test}
base_model <- lm(
  triglyceride ~ age + sex + bmi + race_ethnicity + education + 
                income_ratio + protein + carbs + fiber,
  data = dat_final
)

model_int <- update(base_model, . ~ . + education:carbs)
anova(base_model, model_int)
AIC(base_model, model_int)
```

After running a few separate examples, it seems that the interaction term between education and carbohydrates improves the overall significance of the model the most, with a 0.092 significance level. This indicates that the impact of daily carbohydrate intake on triglycerides may be different for groups with different education levels.

## Data Load for Preliminary

```{r clean-export}
dat_clean <- dat_final %>%
  dplyr::select(-any_of(c("id", "hdl", "ldl", "dbp", "sbp", "sat_fat", "sodium", "potassium", "alcohol")))

write.csv(dat_clean, "nhanes_triglyceride_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)

dim(dat_clean)
```

## Preliminary Model Fitting

```{r prelim-model-fit}
prelim_model <- lm(
  triglyceride ~ age + sex + bmi + race_ethnicity + education + 
                income_ratio + protein + carbs + fiber + 
                education * carbs,
  data = dat_clean
)

summary(prelim_model)
```

## OLS Estimates, Standard Errors, and 95% Confidence Intervals

```{r ols-table-calc}
coef_mat <- summary(prelim_model)$coefficients
ci_mat   <- confint(prelim_model, level = 0.95)

model_table <- data.frame(
  Predictor = rownames(coef_mat),
  Estimate  = round(coef_mat[, "Estimate"], 2),
  SE        = round(coef_mat[, "Std. Error"], 2),
  CI_Lower  = round(ci_mat[, 1], 2),
  CI_Upper  = round(ci_mat[, 2], 2),
  t_stat    = round(coef_mat[, "t value"], 2),
  p_value   = ifelse(coef_mat[, "Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.001, "< 0.001", 
                     round(coef_mat[, "Pr(>|t|)"], 3)),
  row.names = NULL
)

kable(
  model_table,
  caption = paste0("OLS estimates, standard errors, and 95% CIs for preliminary model (n = ", nrow(dat_clean), ").")
)
```

## Residual Analysis and Assumption Check

```{r residual-diagnostic-plots, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
# Reset active devices and set 1 plot per screen
while (dev.cur() > 1) dev.off()
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1.5))

fit <- fitted(prelim_model)
res <- resid(prelim_model)

# 1. Y vs. Fitted Values
plot(fit, dat_clean$triglyceride, pch = 16, cex = 0.8, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Fitted Values (mg/dL)", ylab = "Observed TG (mg/dL)",
     main = "Condition 1: Y vs. Fitted Values")
abline(a = 0, b = 1, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 2. Residuals vs. Fitted
plot(prelim_model, which = 1, col = "steelblue", pch = 16, cex = 0.8,
     caption = "", sub.caption = "")
title(main = "Residuals vs. Fitted")

# 3. Normal Q-Q
plot(prelim_model, which = 2, col = "steelblue", pch = 16, cex = 0.8,
     caption = "", sub.caption = "")
title(main = "Normal Q-Q Plot")

# 4. Residuals vs. Leverage
plot(prelim_model, which = 5, col = "steelblue", pch = 16, cex = 0.8,
     caption = "", sub.caption = "")
title(main = "Residuals vs. Leverage")

# 5. Residuals vs. Age
plot(dat_clean$age, res, pch = 16, cex = 0.8, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Age (years)", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals vs. Age")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 6. Residuals vs. BMI
plot(dat_clean$bmi, res, pch = 16, cex = 0.8, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = expression(BMI~(kg/m^2)), ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals vs. BMI")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 7. Residuals vs. Income Ratio
plot(dat_clean$income_ratio, res, pch = 16, cex = 0.8, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Income-to-Poverty Ratio", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals vs. Income Ratio")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 8. Residuals vs. Protein
plot(dat_clean$protein, res, pch = 16, cex = 0.8, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Protein Intake (g)", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals vs. Protein")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 9. Residuals vs. Carbs
plot(dat_clean$carbs, res, pch = 16, cex = 0.8, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Carbohydrate Intake (g)", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals vs. Carbohydrates")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 10. Residuals vs. Fiber
plot(dat_clean$fiber, res, pch = 16, cex = 0.8, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Fiber Intake (g)", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals vs. Fiber")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 11. Residuals by Sex
boxplot(res ~ dat_clean$sex, col = "lightblue",
        xlab = "Sex", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals by Sex")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 12. Residuals by Race/Ethnicity
boxplot(res ~ dat_clean$race_ethnicity, col = "lightblue",
        xlab = "Race/Ethnicity", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals by Race/Ethnicity",
        las = 2, cex.axis = 0.85)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

# 13. Residuals by Education
boxplot(res ~ dat_clean$education, col = "lightblue",
        xlab = "Education Level", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals by Education Level",
        las = 2, cex.axis = 0.85)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
```
